beats.narration_text: I'm Zhe Liu. This is my game, Walker Survival Shooting. In a subway after the end of the world, the player carries a military tablet everywhere.

beats.narration_text: In one sentence: the player uses the apps on the tablet, above all a memo app, to sort out clues and work out quests. And while the tablet is open, the world does not stop.

beats.narration_text: In Escape from Tarkov, a quest tells you which map, how many to kill, and what to bring back. Many games also tick off each step for you and tell you the next one.

beats.narration_text: In my game, a quest gives only the final goal, like: find this thing for me. You find the clues in the world yourself. Each faction writes its testimony in memos. You copy them into your own memo, compare them, find the holes, and finish the job your own way. This is a design. It is not built yet.

beats.narration_text: I have played each of these for more than a hundred hours: Metal Gear Solid Five, The Phantom Pain, Subnautica, and Abiotic Factor. The Phantom Pain's computer is like an escape menu inside a computer. Subnautica's PDA puts the backpack, the logs and the settings in one place. Abiotic Factor's mail, compendium and recipes are mostly status displays. They rarely turn these into separate apps that act on the world.

beats.narration_text: This is for recruiters and hiring managers. I want to work as a technical game designer. Before you start, read the key table in the README: Tab raises the tablet, hold Tab for two hands, and click the tablet with the mouse. The game has no on-screen hints.

beats.narration_text: Raising the tablet, putting it away, and switching from one hand to two are all run by one state machine. The screen lights only when the tablet is in place, and stays dark if the raise is interrupted.

beats.narration_text: I wrote the screen glow shader by hand. The landing dust is a particle effect. On my laptop GPU, its cost is almost nothing.

beats.narration_text: The screen glow and the effects have automated tests that rerun without a window. I also break the code on purpose, to see whether the tests catch it. The tablet system and the memo app have no tests yet.

beats.narration_text: I write each design rule down first, then turn it into code. For example: with the tablet in both hands, you cannot walk, and every key goes to the tablet. With it in one hand, the keys only control the character.

show.event: Scripted input: W with two hands does not move the body; with one hand it walks (tablet-scripted.mp4 frames 480-673)

qc.contrast_reason: Edge-to-edge engine render or document frame; the essential text is the label strip.

beats.narration_text: For now, this demo has no shooting, extraction or looting. They will come later, but they are not what is new. First I will build the smallest clue loop: open two testimonies, copy, make a new memo, paste, save. When it works, I will record real play, labelled with its version, to show that it runs.

beats.narration_text: The biggest risk is that this game is too big for one person. So I am building only the core idea first, with code that is easy to fix and easy to extend. A friend makes the art on commission.

beats.narration_text: I chose this project mostly to learn. The engine, shaders, particles, animation and Blender were all new to me. I had some programming before, but it did not help much. What I most want to show is gameplay. Art has AI and collaborators to help; gameplay, I have to think up myself.
